article.title: Dynamic Changes of Reproductive Hormones in Male Minipuberty: Temporal Dissociation of Leydig and Sertoli Cell Activity
readLocators: Data availability and three supplement references, printed page 1567

population.description: Healthy term singleton male infants, COPENHAGEN Minipuberty Study 2016–2018, Denmark; source describes Caucasian infants only.

unresolvedSourceLimits: Results describe a TT model median below LOQ around six months; the late graphical center does not reconcile with that wording. No specific author error or correction is assumed.
Results report 6/34 TT samples below LOQ in the entire 340–390-day window. This is not a median, exact-day value or under-one-year-specific denominator.
Two TT fits are described without a sufficient selection/joining rule or original numeric model export; exact handling of low results in fitting remains unclear.
The three official v1 supplements do not supply a numeric TT export or resolve this conflict.
The old day-212 numeric display boundary belongs to the application graphical-readability policy, not a source diagnostic threshold or proof that biological values cease there.

supplements.content: SHBG and calculated free testosterone, not total testosterone export.
SDS variation, not numeric TT age model.
INSL3 group statistics, not numeric TT age model.

insightCitations.location: Supplemental Table 1, LCMSMS hormones sheet, male TT age model 6–18 years
insightCitations.limitation: Cross-sectional chronological-age model, not an individual trajectory or observed peak at ages 20–29.

insightCitations.claim: The highest adult total-testosterone group mean was in 18–29; all older group means were lower.
insightCitations.title: Age-Stratified Reference Ranges for Directly Measured Serum Free Testosterone in Community-Dwelling and Healthy Men
insightCitations.location: Table 1, Total T, nmol/L row; 1194 participants aged 18–86
insightCitations.statistic: arithmetic group mean of total testosterone, despite paper title focused on free testosterone
limitations: All older means are lower than 20.7 nmol/L at 18–29, but the sequence is not strictly decreasing every decade.
Mixed younger healthy and older community cohorts; group differences do not isolate causal aging or predict individual change.
These means are not medians, reference intervals or normal/abnormal thresholds.
